done_when: README.md is about 1,000 words and names only commands that exist in the installed release.

known.title: Gate: Update the tests that read the moved README sections
Include the required Autoreview helper in the setup path
Correct the merge instructions in the linked guide
Correct the default model and effort claims

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a contributor or scheduled CI run executes the full test suite.
The rewrite removes content that existing tests still require in README.md. `tests/test_upgrade_guide.py:18` looks for the removed upgrade heading, `tests/test_score_upgrade.py:135` and `tests/test_journey_guide.py:73` split on removed headings, and `tests/test_proto_docs.py:34` and `tests/test_sales_checklist.py:12` assert links that are no longer present. Those tests fail until their checks follow the content to its new home or otherwise test the revised documentation contract.
findings.title: Gate: Update the tests that read the moved README sections

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a new user follows the setup on a computer without Autoreview and asks Forge to review a code change.
The prerequisites omit Autoreview, and the newly linked non-coder instructions at `docs/start.md:21-24` and `:94` tell the agent to install no additional tool. Yet `src/forge/review.py:799-806` requires the separately installed, pinned helper, and `:964` invokes it for a review; `src/forge/doctor.py:378-380` only reports its absence. The first code review cannot complete using the documented setup.
findings.title: Include the required Autoreview helper in the setup path

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an owner opens the linked merging guide to enable agent merges.
The README correctly directs the owner to run `forge merge enable`, but its new link goes to `docs/guide.md:652-654`, which tells the owner to ask the agent to change `merge` in a fix. The shipped agent instructions at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:348-351` expressly prohibit that action and direct the owner to the terminal command instead. Following the linked instructions therefore cannot enable agent merging.
findings.title: Correct the merge instructions in the linked guide

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a repo owner changes the cold-read or task-review limit to one round.
The new reference page says `forge.toml` can change both the fix and task review limits, but `src/forge/close.py:412` fixes the fix limit at one and only reads a setting for tasks. It also says at line 90 that a cold read stops after round two; the moved journey at `docs/guide.md:242-244` makes the same unconditional two-round claims. `src/forge/story.py:200` uses the configured cold-read limit, so these instructions give owners the wrong expectations for supported settings.
findings.title: Correct the documented review-round settings

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a new repo uses only Claude, or a team starts a user-facing change.
A Claude-only setup sets `tools = "claude"` in `src/forge/init.py:182-185`; its plan reads and reviews use the Claude Sonnet entries at `:124-126` and `:136-138`, rather than Codex at max. The next paragraph also says every first build starts at low effort, but `src/forge/worker.py:182-221` routes user-facing work through the design settings, which start at high or xhigh. The ruling about which tool reviews when both are installed does not cover these cases.
findings.title: Correct the default model and effort claims

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - a maintainer checks the proof that every command in the rewritten README exists.
The recorded proof says the README names no Forge command and checks the old command table, but the reviewed README now contains `forge merge enable`. That proof would also pass if this newly named command did not exist, so it does not establish the command portion of Done-when. The command is implemented by the installed release, but the recorded check needs to cover the actual README at this head.
findings.title: Gate: proof list

why: The README misses releases v1.2.27 to v1.2.41, names a command that does not exist, and gives wrong statements about who builds, what must be installed and how many plan reads run.
